brief.title: Interviewing a candidate — HR Manager (B1)
constraints: Employment-law-adjacent statements kept generic; no legal procedure claims (D-U11)

exponents: What is most important to you in this role?
What help do you need to finish the task?
Which option would work best for you, and why?
L0|CFN-0035|B1.notes: Ask clear questions that help the other person explain a need or preference.

exponents: Can you tell me about your previous role?
What happened after you spoke to the team?
Could you explain how you completed that task?
L0|CFN-0011|B1.notes: Ask for relevant details using direct, polite questions.

L1|STM-0143.description: An interviewer asks a candidate about relevant experience, work examples and expectations. They use questions to gather information and identify the candidate's needs, ask follow-up questions where needed, and close with a clear description of the next contact rather than an unsupported hiring promise.
flow: Establish the focus of the interview conversation.
Ask about relevant experience and a specific example.
Follow up to clarify the candidate's contribution and priorities.
Clarify what is known about the next contact.
variationPoints: Stakeholders involved in the selection conversation.
B1 direct questions versus B2 probing and clarification.
Industry-specific constraints supplied by the later context overlay.

L2|CM-11.summary: Communicate priorities, decisions and performance expectations across people and teams. Gather relevant information, consider options, explain decisions and responsibilities, and review agreed outcomes. Use evidence and respectful questioning to understand performance gaps. Management responsibility and language proficiency remain separate: the same decision may need simpler or more developed English depending on the learner.

communicationMoves.move: Set the discussion purpose and priorities.
Gather relevant information and summarise the situation.
Discuss options and their trade-offs.
Explain the decision and its reasoning.
Agree ownership and action points.
Discuss performance gaps and practical support.
Review progress against agreed goals.

qualityCriteria: The purpose and priorities are clear to participants.
Actions have understood owners and review points.
Performance discussion uses specific evidence rather than personal labels.
English difficulty reflects the specified CEFR level, not the job title.

responsibilities: Clarify recruitment needs with the relevant department head.
Ask candidates for relevant experience and specific work examples.
Discuss role expectations and onboarding questions using confirmed workplace information.
Respond to employee queries and clarify information that is uncertain.
Discuss performance gaps with evidence and invite the employee's explanation.
Hear employee concerns respectfully and identify an appropriate next conversation.
Explain agreed workplace decisions or policies without adding unconfirmed rules.
Summarise actions, ownership and review points.

jobKnowledge.title: Recruitment conversation
jobKnowledge.text: An HR conversation gathers information about the role and the candidate's relevant experience. The examples and work constraints come from the industry context; the shared role core does not assume one sector.

jobKnowledge.title: Performance evidence
jobKnowledge.text: A performance gap is a difference between an agreed expectation and observed work. The manager's English should distinguish that evidence from assumptions about the employee's attitude or personal circumstances.

jobKnowledge.title: Employee concerns
jobKnowledge.text: An employee may need information, support or a further conversation. The manager can listen, clarify the concern and explain a known next contact without promising confidentiality or an outcome beyond their authority.

jobKnowledge.title: Policy communication
jobKnowledge.text: Explain only confirmed workplace information supplied in the situation. Do not invent employment rules, legal entitlements or disciplinary procedures.

jobKnowledge.title: Agreed follow-up
jobKnowledge.text: A clear summary identifies the actions discussed, the people responsible and any agreed review point. It does not imply that a conversation alone settles a recruitment decision or employee concern.

brief.title: Addressing underperformance — HR Manager (B1)
constraints: Employment-law-adjacent statements kept generic; no disciplinary-procedure claims (D-U11)

exponents: The report was late twice this week; what happened?
What is making it difficult to meet the agreed target?
Let us agree on a plan and check progress next week.
L0|CFN-0070|B1.notes: Name a specific performance gap, ask about the cause and agree on a next step.

L1|STM-0127.description: A manager discusses an observable gap between agreed expectations and an employee's work. They describe the gap without personal accusations, hear the employee's explanation, discuss support, and agree on practical improvements and a review point. The exchange does not prescribe disciplinary procedures.
flow: State the agreed expectation and a specific observed gap.
Agree on practical improvements and responsibilities.
Confirm a review point and summarise the agreement.
variationPoints: The task, evidence and agreed performance expectation.
The employee's explanation and available support.
The manager's actual authority to agree actions.
B1 straightforward wording versus B2 nuanced discussion.
Workplace-specific consequences described without legal or disciplinary claims.

L2|CM-10.summary: Coordinate a team's immediate work through briefings, clear task ownership, progress checks and everyday feedback. Invite questions, identify obstacles, and confirm handovers or revised arrangements. Keep the focus on the work and the support needed. Team supervision concerns day-to-day coordination; broader decisions and formal performance conversations belong to the management module.

communicationMoves.move: Brief the team on the immediate work.
Clarify each task and its owner.
Check understanding and invite questions.
Ask for progress and identify obstacles.
Give specific everyday feedback and agree practical support.
Confirm the handover and remaining actions.

qualityCriteria: Team members understand the immediate task and owner.
Questions and obstacles receive a clear response.
Updates identify completed, ongoing or blocked work.
Handovers explain what remains and who will follow up.

pilot.purpose: Architecture-validation prototype approved by the author on 4 October 2026. Not for publication. Final state may never be COMPILED or PUBLISHED.

policies.D-U11: Job knowledge only to make communication realistic; not certification. No invented safety instructions, public procedures or legal/medical/financial advice. Factual claims in regulated areas must be traceable; U-1 avoids them.
policies.D-U12: Hybrid characters: role-specific realistic characters and reusable stakeholder archetypes; no single permanent character; Arif is not used.
policies.D-U14: Learning cycle for new role content: Context → Notice → Understand → Guided Practice → Role Practice → Performance Task → Feedback → Review/Retrieval. Not claimed to exist in the current book.
policies.D-U07: Vocabulary: propose terms only; the repository assigns V-<SCOPE>-<NUMBER> codes and reuses existing codes. Never invent codes.
policies.D-U10: Generate only the requested delta. Do not regenerate objects supplied in context.

style.currency: Indian rupees (₹) unless the situation requires otherwise
style.names: realistic South Asian names by default; international names where the context has them; no stereotypes
style.brands: no real company or brand names; use generic descriptions (e.g. 'the delivery app', 'the dealership')
style.languages: English only. No Bengali or Hindi script or transliteration in U-1.
style.audio: None. Content must be fully usable as text (D-U06).

context.review: Output is stored as GENERATED, then AI QA, then Editorial Review by the author. Specialist and native review are NOT_REQUIRED for U-1. It is never published.

instructions: Return ONE JSON object only (no prose, no Markdown fences), conforming to the response format in 'responseFormat'.
Produce exactly the outputs listed in 'expectedOutputs', using their tempId, type and key unchanged.
Generate only these outputs. Do not regenerate objects given in 'context' — use them.
Do not invent IDs or vocabulary codes. Reference existing codes only as given in context; propose new vocabulary with tempIds.
English only: no Bengali/Hindi script or transliteration. No audio references. No real brand or company names.
No legal, medical, financial or safety advice; no invented procedures or rules (D-U11).
Report honestly in selfCheck: 'met', 'not met' or 'uncertain'. Never claim approval, certification or CEFR validation.
